clause_inventory.coverage: Both original numbered paragraphs fully covered; paragraph 1 split at Provided, however to isolate displaced limitation; preamble, signature and neighboring page text not operative units.

savings_reasoning: No continuing independent command of EO 9452 is identified within the complete original, actual amendment, contextual EO 9521, complete revoker, and accepted numbered-order/current-law searches. Paragraph 2 reserves independently applicable Federal Register publication law; it does not create that law or a separate post-revocation command. EO 9514 reenacts the grant and modifies its limitation, without a saving. EO 12292 expressly revokes the order effective February 15, 1981 without a target-specific saving. EO 9521 saves nonrevival of other listed orders; EO 9452 is authority in its preamble and is not in that list. The April 1945 State regulation is a historical exercise of authority, not a later revival of the delegation. This finding concerns continuing commands of this order and does not assert that revocation invalidated completed acts, accrued legal positions, or every regulation formerly issued under its authority. No post-revocation numbered-order use or current-law predicate identified in the bounded searches requires treating such an act as a continuing EO 9452 command.
chronology_reasoning: EO 9452 creates an indefinite Foreign Service regulatory delegation and a publication delegation, subject to the original broad prohibition where the President has specific statutory rulemaking authority and to independent publication law. The complete high-confidence official extract contains no own-term expiry, report-triggered cessation or unaccounted operative provision. Paragraph 1 is split into its grant and proviso because EO 9514, signed January 18, 1945 without delayed effectiveness, reenacts the grant but narrows the proviso to permit exercise of Revised Statutes section 1752 authority. The original unqualified proviso therefore first ends in its original form on January 18, 1945; the grant, remaining limitation in its amended form, and paragraph 2 continue. EO 9521 is not a revoker of this target: its preamble acknowledges EO 9452 as amended and its revocation list names other orders. The actual 1945 State regulation discovered in a neighboring-document extract is a use of the amended delegation, not evidence of cessation or revival. EO 12292 section 10(a) revokes EO 9452, and section 11 expressly makes that action effective as of February 15, 1981, rather than its February 23 signature or February 25 publication. This is the last end among the original operative units. The sole current USC mention reproduces that revocation and supplies no continuing predicate. Strong complete official extracts plus matching official GPO fixity establish the read text; no PDF page image verification is asserted. The provisional whole-order status remains no.
